claims.claim: AMD disclosed an agreement signed September 26 to acquire World Labs for approximately $8.2 billion in AMD shares, subject to adjustments; closing remains conditional.
contradictions: An agreement is not a completed acquisition; performance and open-model benefits were not demonstrated.

claims.claim: AP reports that the voluntary US accord calls for company controls, an independent external auditor and board-committee review of auditor reports.
contradictions: The signed text was not located; auditor powers and release authority are unverified.
AP reports Dario Amodei said the risk-addressing mechanism remained under discussion.

claims.claim: A complaint dated September 29 concerning OpenAI agents’ access to Hugging Face systems was filed; WIRED reports an alleged California computer-access-law violation.
entities: Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology
contradictions: The complaint is an allegation, not a judicial finding; no ruling appears in the supplied evidence.

claims.claim: OpenAI announced Dots for ongoing work and computer use in the Agents API, with specified product and workspace access restrictions.
contradictions: No independent long-horizon reliability or production permission-control assessment was supplied.

claims.claim: OpenAI announced a Luna-based Decisions API in limited preview and plans for broader release in the coming days.
contradictions: The API is not yet broadly released in the supplied evidence; calibration was not independently established.

claims.claim: OpenAI lists GPT-6.1 Sol at $2 per million standard input tokens, $0.10 per million cached input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
contradictions: Token prices do not establish cost per successful task.

claims.claim: OpenAI reports a 6.4-percentage-point DeepSWE v1.1 gain and a seven-percentage-point OSWorld 2.0 offline-set gain under different effort settings.
contradictions: The setups differ and were not independently verified as production task-success results.

claims.claim: Ollama announced /v1/systemone for typed decisions and listed Nimble 9B and two experimental Tev1 variants.
contradictions: The Tev1 variants are experimental; planned cloud models were not announced as available.

claims.claim: Ollama reports 91 milliseconds per decision for Nimble 9B in one local Pac-Man example on an M5 Max and cites a comparison spanning 13 datasets and 3,880 decisions.
contradictions: One machine and example do not establish general latency; one comparison model’s results came from a separate run.

claims.claim: Microsoft reports using Quine to prioritize thousands of compounds for pancreatic-cancer cell-state assays; its highest-ranked compounds produced the largest intended shifts in the reported experiments.
contradictions: The reverse shift was harder; no independent replication, treatment effect or patient outcome was established.

A legal complaint is not a finding of liability.
No independent production evaluation was supplied for Dots, GPT-6.1 Sol, Ollama’s decision models or Quine.

Retain open: no Anthropic-specific selection, escalation, publication or stop-authority details were verified.
Retain experimental: Dots’ described permissions and visibility do not establish delegated authority and customer-controlled telemetry for the proposed registry.
Retain high confidence without declaring the thesis met; the required combination was not verified at two platforms.
Retain high confidence unchanged; AMD’s agreement is not direct evidence about NVIDIA’s rack architecture.
Quine adds a reported wet-lab loop, with general reproducibility and clinical utility unverified.
GPT-6.1 Sol warrants local routing tests, not an assumed improvement in cost per successful task.

Coding agents and serving economics: GPT-6.1 Sol calls for pinned task-cost comparisons.

Open-weight models and local inference: Ollama lists three local decision models.
Enterprise strategy: AMD’s proposed acquisition links model research with infrastructure.
AI governance: the voluntary accord needs a published text and documented auditor authority.
builder_actions: Specify permissions, approvals, logs and task-level success criteria before piloting persistent or computer-using agents.
Compare GPT-6.1 Sol on pinned tasks using successful-task cost, latency, effort and tool configuration.
Test typed decisions on labeled, low-stakes cases, including calibration and escalation.
Track Quine protocols and independent replication rather than infer clinical utility.
Track the accord’s signed text and auditor powers; preserve explicit network authority and incident records for agents.

continuity_reviews.assessment: Retain open. A September 11 Reuters report described negotiations, but this review did not establish a newly published draft or substantive framework by September 30. The voluntary White House accord is a different mechanism.

Retain confirmed from the prior review; this dossier found no basis to revise that status. The new voluntary accord should not be conflated with operational details for permanently embedded evaluators.
Retain progress. The accord describes a concrete review structure, but its voluntary status and the unverified powers of external auditors do not establish a binding release threshold.
Retain open. The industry accord supplies no verified Anthropic-specific evaluator-selection, escalation, publication or stop-authority details.

Retain experimental. OpenAI’s Dots announcement describes app permissions, custom rules and activity visibility, but does not establish the delegated-authority and customer-controlled telemetry requirements of the proposed internal registry.

Retain high confidence without declaring the thesis met. Dots adds customer-facing rules and visibility, but this review did not verify the full runtime-policy and customer-controlled-telemetry combination at two major platforms.
Retain high confidence unchanged. AMD’s World Labs agreement concerns a competing company’s model-research strategy, not direct evidence about NVIDIA’s third-party-accelerator rack architecture.

Microsoft’s Quine account adds a reported model-to-wet-lab prioritization loop. Retain the verification bottleneck: the selected experiments do not establish general reproducibility or clinical utility.
GPT-6.1 Sol warrants a new routing comparison, but OpenAI’s benchmark and price claims do not replace workload-specific successful-task cost measurements.

The California complaint adds a legal-accountability question to the existing runtime-boundary storyline. It does not change the previously reported sandbox measurements or prove the complaint’s allegations.
